title: Warehouse-Loss Case Decisions at the FBN Reimbursement Desk
content:
**Desk standard, Fulfilled by Northloop (FBN).** This standard fixes the units the support desk approves when it decides a seller's open warehouse-loss case, the reimbursement case whose loss kind is lost in warehouse; the approved units become the unit count of the case and the reimbursement run pays them afterwards.

**When the approved units are fixed.** The units approved on a warehouse-loss case are fixed only after the units claimed on that case equal the claimable lost units of its SKU. Put the other way round: as long as the units claimed on the case differ from the claimable lost units of the case's SKU, the units approved on it are not yet fixed.

## Effect of a decision

| Before the decision | After the decision |
|---|---|
| Case status submitted (open) | Case status approved |
| Unit count of the case: the units claimed | Unit count of the case: the units approved |
| No reimbursement | Reimbursement of the approved units by Northloop's reimbursement run, issued separately afterwards |

## The decision tool

**Tool:** `approve_lost_inventory_case_b95e2fef`

This is a support-desk tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. One call marks the case approved and sets the unit count on the case to the units Northloop accepts for reimbursement, re-recording the loss kind, source references and SKU of the decision. The tool itself makes no payment.

### Parameters

- `case_id` — reference number of the seller's open FBN reimbursement case being decided, as shown in the seller's case list from the FBN case lookup (identifier).
- `reimbursement_type` — loss kind recorded on the case, one of: `lost_in_warehouse` (units went missing inside a fulfillment center), `damaged_in_warehouse` (units damaged inside a fulfillment center), `inbound_shortage` (an inbound shipment line received short), `customer_return_not_received` (a refunded buyer return never arrived), `removal_lost` (a removal shipment to the seller was lost), `not_applicable` (the case is a fee dispute rather than a loss claim).
- `adjustment_ref` — inventory adjustment reference the case names, copied from the case record; empty string when the case names no single adjustment.
- `shipment_id` — inbound shipment number the case names, copied from the case record; empty string when it names none.
- `order_id` — marketplace order number the case names, copied from the case record; empty string when it names none.
- `removal_order_id` — removal order reference the case names, copied from the case record; empty string when it names none.
- `sku` — seller SKU the case is about, copied character for character from the case record (verbatim).
- `units_approved` — number of units approved for reimbursement on the case: a whole number of units, zero or more, with no fractional part.

### Return

A receipt with `case_id`, `sku`, `units_approved` (the units approved, now shown as the case's unit count) and `case_status`, always `approved`. A returned receipt means the approval is recorded. The tool defines no other outcome.

## Basis questions

*Does the desk pay the seller when it decides the case?* No. The decision records the approved units; the reimbursement run pays them afterwards.

*Can the approved units be zero?* Yes. The tool accepts zero or more units, and zero approved units is a recorded decision like any other.
